clue.text: Irritating party turning out craft for river

indicators.note: turning out means evicting one group of letters so another can take its place

parts.note: taken as the word itself
craft means art or skill
the Esk is a river in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A tiresome group throws a boat off the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PARTY, remove ART (craft) and put ESK (a river) in its place; 'for' marks the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something pesky is annoying or troublesome.

clue.text: Devastate Troy and perish? It — happened long ago

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: the stuff that happened long ago

indicators.note: to devastate is to lay waste, so the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: The fall of Troy, with its city ravaged and people dying, belongs to the distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: The sack of Troy is legend from before written records, so the whole clue also hints at the answer; the dash separates the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The era before written records covers everything that happened in the remote past.

clue.text: In part it's a convenient container for yolk

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: An eggshell is praised as handy packaging for the yellow centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Biology term: the yolk sac is the membrane pouch holding an embryo's food supply.

clue.text: One who cries out, being commonly cowardly?

definitions.meaning: in informal, nonstandard speech 'yellow' (cowardly) is pronounced and written with an -er ending

explanation.surface: Someone who shouts a lot is accused, in rough speech, of lacking nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouter is literally one who yells, and colloquial American 'yeller' means yellow, i.e. gutless.

clue.text: Performer still around to entertain City University

indicators.note: to entertain is to host a guest within, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: extant means still in existence
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: An entertainer still on the scene is booked for a show at a London university.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: an executant is one who carries out or performs, especially a musician.

clue.text: Swear-word? The writer's left in old favourite for a start

indicators.note: for a start puts the old favourite piece at the front, before the writer's piece
in places the abbreviation inside the other piece

parts.note: an ex-pet is a former pet, a favourite of old
the writer refers to the setter, so 'the writer's' is I'VE (I have)

explanation.surface: A writer admits having cursed, starting from a beloved old phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' is read as 'the writer has', I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive is an oath or curse; the question mark admits it need not be one word.

clue.text: Select friar lacking vehicle and money initially

indicators.note: lacking signals that letters go missing from the friar's name

parts.note: a Carmelite is a friar of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A chosen monk has neither a car nor cash to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CAR and M from CARMELITE.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, select means choice or exclusive, the best of a group.

clue.text: New team leader made run somehow: it's not imagined

definitions.note: read as a clause: something that somehow never came to mind

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters that follow
leader picks out the first letter of team

explanation.surface: A fresh captain makes a run in some unexpected way, beyond anyone's dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges T (team leader) with MADE and RUN. 'somehow' could also be read as a second anagram signal, but one is enough, so it is taken with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never conceived of in a dream is beyond imagining; read 'it's' as the answer standing for it.

clue.text: A drink a day, up to the time of a party

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
till means until
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A daily tipple taken right up until the party starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Amontillado is a medium-dry sherry, so a kind of drink.

clue.text: Footslog bringing soldiers into outskirts of Tobruk

indicators.note: into places the soldiers between the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of Tobruk are used

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A wartime march in which troops approach the Libyan port of Tobruk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trek is a long, arduous journey on foot, a slog.

clue.text: Typical reforms dogging European Union oil producers

indicators.note: dogging means following closely, so the shuffled word comes after the abbreviations
reforms means remakes, so the word's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Standard reforms hound Europe's bloc, which produces oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: gum trees yield eucalyptus oil, so they are oil producers.

clue.text: Mob advancing rapidly at first in ferry port

indicators.note: advancing moves a letter forward, and 'rapidly at first' names that letter as R

parts.note: Dover is the main English ferry port for France

explanation.surface: A crowd surges in a Channel ferry town.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the Kent port; moving its R forward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a drove is a herd or crowd moving together.

clue.text: Happily placed, surrounded by own gold, for example

definitions.meaning: comfortable and doing what suits one

definitions.text: surrounded by own gold, for example
definitions.meaning: gold is a chemical element, so being surrounded by your own one is being literally amid your element

explanation.surface: Someone content and rich, encircled by their own gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in your element means being in congenial surroundings, comfortable and suited.

clue.text: Leave far behind? Not in aloofness

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
distance can mean coolness or reserve

explanation.surface: Is a standoffish manner the way to get away from people?
explanation.definitionFit: To outdistance rivals is to get well ahead of them, leaving them trailing.

clue.text: Plant producing female clothing worn by male actor?

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
on means being worn
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: A plant appears to come from a man in a frock on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the dragon tree, Dracaena draco, is a Canary Islands tree yielding dragon's blood resin.

clue.text: Very exaggerated-sounding wear for ballerina

indicators.note: sounding says the result is how a phrase is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: too-too is a dated expression for excessive or overdone

explanation.surface: An over-the-top dancer's costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too-too', an affected old phrase for 'extreme', when spoken matches the skirt's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the stiff short skirt is a dancer's classic costume.

clue.text: One covers up bird mess scattered round most of meadow

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters surround the trimmed field
scattered tells us to spread these letters into a new order
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: Someone hides bird droppings spread across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' gives DISSEMBR from BIRD MESS; 'round' puts it around LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: a dissembler conceals true motives or feelings, so is someone who hides things.

clue.text: Cut across peak astride horse or cow

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the shorn piece holds the rest within

parts.note: shorn means cut, like sheared wool

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the hill's letters sit either side of the drug's letter

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A rider takes a shortcut over the hilltop, straddling a horse or a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Shorthorn is a breed of cattle, so a type of cow.

clue.text: At sea level, perhaps, regularly play amid Hereford's noise?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: a Hereford is a cattle breed and cattle make a lowing sound

indicators.note: regularly selects every other letter

explanation.surface: Music playing on and off among mooing cattle in a flat landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: land at sea level is flat and close to the ground, the 'perhaps' showing it as one instance.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type with money vexed about retiring

parts.note: rhino is old British slang for money

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: sore means vexed or annoyed
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A tough rich person gets cross and withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' reverses SORE + C to give CEROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and figurative: the animal's hide is thick, and a thick-skinned person is called one too.

clue.text: Speak at length? Not on drug injection

indicators.note: not means leave off the following word

parts.note: to bang on is to go on and on talking

explanation.surface: A long rant against injecting drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a bang is a shot of a narcotic.

clue.text: Senior cleric unceasingly displaying polish

parts.note: Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A top churchman always displays a refined manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: veneer is a thin surface layer or superficial gloss, like polish.

clue.text: Hamlet would not participate in such general gossip?

definitions.text: Hamlet would not participate in such general gossip?

parts.words: Hamlet would not participate in such general gossip?
parts.note: a hamlet is a village too small to be a town, so it could never share in what a bigger settlement chatters about

explanation.surface: The Prince of Denmark refuses to join in the gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like Shakespeare's prince; it is a small village, which is not a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the subject everyone in the community is discussing.

clue.text: Best available tonic?

parts.note: out can mean released or on sale, as of a book
doh, the first note of a sol-fa scale, is the tonic

explanation.surface: Is this the finest pick-me-up you can buy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' is the musical keynote, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a verb, best means beat or surpass.

clue.text: Go away, missing end of sporting expedition

indicators.note: missing end of tells us the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a shoot is a party out hunting game birds

explanation.surface: Clear off, the hunt has lost its ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: a cry used to send someone or something packing.

clue.text: A small number sheltering in Hawaii's capital

indicators.note: sheltering means holding within, so the outer letters go round the rest

parts.note: HI is the US postal code for Hawaii
No is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A few people take refuge in Honolulu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawaii's capital' looks like one phrase meaning Honolulu; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Gardener to Sam or Tony fencing in run

indicators.note: fencing in means enclosing, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Sam Weller and his father Tony are characters in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A gardener to either of two men puts a fence round a dog run.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: someone who uses a trowel, a small garden tool.

clue.text: Emitter of light sometimes associated with Zeppelin

definitions.meaning: the rock band name pairs this word with Zeppelin

explanation.surface: An airship, glowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of light-emitting diode, and the first word of the rock band Led Zeppelin.

clue.text: Exaggerate distress, say, finding garden in this state?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: a garden that has run wild

indicators.note: say signals that what follows is spoken, matching a word of different spelling

parts.note: to over-groan would be to moan excessively

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes their anguish on seeing an untended garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden left untended becomes covered with rampant weeds and plants.

clue.text: Travel on horseback across key elevation

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the riding word encloses the note

parts.note: to ride is to travel on horseback
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Riding over an important piece of high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised stretch of land, a crest.
